text:
Anna (PM): Quick sync — we need a short customer-ready launch checklist for Private (customer-managed networking). One page. Who signs what, and which gates block GA?

Raj (Eng): +1. From eng: rolling non-destructive upgrades, clear rollback path, preflight with actionable errors, signed artifacts for airgap.

Marta (Field): Field wants a hard "Network Handover Form" customers sign before dry-run. It must list ASN, egress pool, DNS owner, and maintenance window. Otherwise we get blame for BGP mistakes.

Kyle (NetOps): NetOps requires a BGP handoff dry-run that proves egress-IP continuity and AS-path validation. Installer must emit an egress->node mapping (JSON) we can reconcile. Dry-run signed by customer network owner is required.

Jia (SRE): Observability: minimal set = upgrade_status, upgrade_progress_pct, agent_versions, node_egress_ips, postcutover_error_rate. Need event timeline that ties to operator actions. Telemetry toggles must respect customer KMS and allow sanitization before upload.

Ben (Solutions): Add a short commercial note: we include up to 3 hours of operator-assisted cutover per contract; anything beyond is billable at the contracted hourly rate. Customers need to opt into assisted mode in writing.

Leah (Legal): Please add a short "Limits of Liability" bullet for the one-pager: we do not accept responsibility for misconfigured customer infra or third-party network appliances. Keep legal language short and non-technical.

Anna (PM): Draft bullets for the one-pager (short):
- Preflight: network reachability, required ports, kernel/disk checks, NAT/iptables scan, egress mapping verified by customer
- Dry-run: BGP handoff simulation + egress continuity verification (NetOps sign-off required)
- Packaging: online installer + sha256-signed airgap bundle; artifact integrity check required
- Upgrade: rolling agents with configurable canary (default 10%), non-destructive; can resume from last good state
- Rollback: documented, timeboxed rollback path; rollback script + checklist to restore prior agent + ip mapping
- Observability: minimal metrics & event timeline; telemetry opt-out; KMS-aware keying + sanitization steps
- Support: up to 3h included operator-assisted cutover; extra hours billable; P1 triage during agreed window
- Customer responsibilities: assign named network owner, provide ASN/IP ranges, open firewall windows, approve dry-run and sign Network Handover Form
- Exclusions: misconfigured BGP, broken physical hardware, unsupported kernel mods, third-party black box NATs

Marta (Field): Add signoff snippet and an example Handover Form paragraph. Keep it short.

Raj (Eng): Also add a mandatory automated preflight exit code map (0=ok, 2=warn, 3=fail) and human-friendly remediation for each non-zero. Ill own that.

Kyle (NetOps): I'll produce the dry-run checklist + verifier script (bgp summary, traceroute checks from probes, curl with --interface, compare egress mapping JSON). NetOps sign-off is a required gate.

Jia (SRE): I'll own metrics schema + event-timeline format and a 1-page troubleshooting playbook for top 4 failure modes. Also include a short privacy step: "run sanitizer.sh before any telemetry leaves customer network."

Leah (Legal): For signoff: include a short acceptance line the customer signs: "Network Owner certifies ASN/IP plan and approves the dry-run." Keep it simple. I can draft the exact wording.

Anna (PM): GA gating question: do we require N customer-verified cutovers before GA? I propose: two successful cutovers on distinct topologies (one on-prem BGP, one VPC/cloud), each exercising rollback at least once, and one performed under constrained-control-plane (airgap-like) conditions.

Marta (Field): Strong yes. Field wants >=2 topologies demonstrated before GA comms.

Raj (Eng): Agreed. Define "successful": preflight green, dry-run pass, canary->full upgrade, rollback executed without IP drift, metrics stable for 48h, signed post-cutover report by field + netowner.

Kyle (NetOps): Also require NetOps signoff after each cutover. One cutover must validate operator-assisted mode and one must be self-service.

Ben (Solutions): We'll include a scheduling template and an example communications plan (1-week pre-notice, confirmation 24h before, 15-min cadence during window). Ill draft the template.

Anna (PM): Owners: Raj = preflight exit codes & rollback docs; Kyle = dry-run checklist & verifier; Jia = metrics & runbook; Marta = Handover Form + customer-facing FAQ; Ben = scheduling template; Leah = signoff wording. I'll collate into a 1-pager and internal checklist by COB Thu.

Marta (Field): Quick FAQ items to add: 1) "What if DNS TTLs are long?" — answer: expect extended dual-path traffic; recommend lowering TTL to 60s when possible. 2) "What if customer devices rewrite source IPs?" — answer: that's an exclusion and must be documented pre-cutover.

Raj (Eng): One more technical note for the one-pager: we will provide an optional IP-preservation test harness that runs a simulated failover and produces a report. It's opt-in and requires customer test IPs.

Anna (PM): Nice. Add that to the bullets as an "optional test harness" line.

deploy-bot: New doc uploaded: /docs/private-deploy/network-handover-onepager-v1.md (internal)

Marta (Field): Will review the draft and add two real-customer FAQ examples. :eyes:
